summary:
FireGuard is an evidence\-based decision\-support platform that helps users explore NASA combustion research for future space missions.

As human exploration expands to the Moon, Mars, and beyond, fire safety decisions require trustworthy and traceable evidence. FireGuard connects mission scenarios with NASA combustion experiment metadata, helping users understand what evidence exists, how it relates to a scenario, and where critical knowledge gaps remain.

Instead of generating unsupported answers, FireGuard uses a fail\-closed approach. When available evidence cannot justify a conclusion, the system explicitly reports insufficient evidence and explains why.

By combining evidence traceability, interactive knowledge exploration, and mission\-context analysis, FireGuard helps make NASA combustion research more accessible, transparent, and actionable for future exploration planning.
details:
Challenge Alignment

Challenge Alignment

This project addresses the challenge of helping users understand and interpret NASA microgravity combustion research. FireGuard organizes experiment information, evidence references, and research relationships into a transparent workflow that helps users explore available knowledge, identify evidence gaps, and better understand fire behaviour research for future human spaceflight.

NASA has produced decades of valuable fire and combustion research through experiments conducted in microgravity environments. However, the information is often distributed across multiple experiments and sources, making it difficult to evaluate within mission-specific contexts.

FireGuard helps users trace available research, understand evidence limitations, identify knowledge gaps, and explore how combustion research may relate to future lunar, Martian, and deep-space mission planning.

What Does FireGuard Do?

FireGuard is an evidence-readiness and fire-safety decision-support platform designed around NASA combustion research. It helps users understand how available research relates to mission scenarios and clearly identifies situations where evidence is insufficient to support a conclusion.

How Does It Work?

The platform combines several connected capabilities:

  • Mission scenario assessment
  • Evidence matching
  • Deterministic assessment generation
  • Evidence traceability
  • Knowledge graph exploration
  • Mission impact analysis

Users begin by reviewing a mission scenario. FireGuard then searches available research metadata, evaluates evidence coverage, and produces a deterministic assessment. Every result can be traced through an evidence chain to related experiment records and source references.

The interactive knowledge graph shows how experiments, evidence records, mission concepts, and research resources relate to one another.

Key Benefits

  • Improves transparency
  • Highlights evidence gaps
  • Encourages scientifically cautious decision-making
  • Supports research traceability
  • Helps planners connect research to mission needs

Design Principle

FireGuard fails closed.

If evidence is missing or too weak, FireGuard reports "Insufficient Evidence" instead of generating unsupported conclusions. Making uncertainty visible rather than hiding it is the platform's core principle.

Intended Impact

Future space missions will require trustworthy safety decisions. FireGuard demonstrates how combustion research can be made more accessible, traceable, and understandable for decision-makers without relying on opaque AI-generated conclusions.

Technologies Used

  • Next.js
  • TypeScript
  • Tailwind CSS
  • shadcn/ui
  • Vitest
  • ESLint

Creativity

Many systems focus on generating answers. FireGuard focuses on generating accountability.

Rather than producing unsupported conclusions, the platform exposes evidence gaps, research limitations, and uncertainty so users can make better-informed decisions based on available NASA research.
